text_fidelity_a:
Dominion 2nd Edition | Deckbuilding Strategy Game for 2-4 Players, Ages 13+ | Updated Cards, Artwork, Streamlined Rules This is the best deck building game EVER!!
I am in my 20's and have only recently been introduced to deck building games, and instantly fell in love.
DOminion and the DC Comic deck games are my favorite, but Dominion provides a larger variety because the cards used change.
The game its self comes with several possible versions of the game.
For example, the game is plaid with several action card decks to draw from, but Dominion comes with twice as many action cards. So, no game is exactly alike. The rule book comes with various options of which action cards to play with for certain kinds of games.
This game is dynamic!

I first played Dominion at a bar with board games. After a few times I fell in love and bought this second edition. The cards are beautiful, more colorful than the first edition. (I attached some photos to see to see the cards)

It says that the game can be played in about 30 minutes... for me it takes closer to an hour with 3 players. It also probably depends on what type of game you play (which actions cards to choose to play with) But because we are still learning, maybe we go a little slower, constantly re reading what the action cards say/do.

At the end of the game, who ever has the most victory points wins.
text_fidelity_b: Dominion 2nd Edition | Deckbuilding Strategy Game for 2-4 Players, Ages 13+ | Updated Cards, Artwork, Streamlined Rules

Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+ Venn is a party game that plays a large number of players, and it comes with a competitive mode and a cooperative mode. The cooperative mode was not fun for our family, so we'll focus on the competitive game. In this game, you use cards with odd artwork to get your teammates to guess a set of three out of twelve possible games. The cards go in one of the seven different sections of a three-way Venn Diagram like you used to see in school. Using the clues you're given, you attempt to identify the three chosen words that the card placer is going for.

There are some fun times to be had here, but a few problems as well. The art is meant to be odd and unusual, but a good amount of it is just plain bad - characters are off-center, objects look like they're floating in the background, etc - and the cards are hard to use because they don't actually fit inside the sections of the Venn diagram. The words are usually very descriptive, but there are also some bad word chocies in the deck like "great" or "interesting" which could literally mean anything.

Unfortunately, this is competing in a crowded market - competitive, team-based family games have been done to death, so if you want to stand out, choose a game like Codenames or Just One or So Clover or...well, there's a lot of them, and they're mostly better than this.
text_fidelity_b: Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+

It’s kind of “odd” because the color is different in the pictures (the picture of the girl holding it makes it look white with a little tan and black splotches. . . which it is not). The one that I received looks like different shades of tan with some dark splotches. Not the least bit pink. . . not the least bit attractive. I understand that not all pigs are pink in real life. . . and not all pings are “pretty”. . . but when you’re making a toy, then the majority of the time they are pink. . . and they should be at least “not-ugly”, which this one is. . . ugly.

The pictures show the pig standing. This pig does not stand. It lays flat down, with the legs forward. There is nothing stiff in the legs so that it can stand, and it’s obviously made to lay flat.

The “puppet part”. There is a “slit” in the bellow where you put four fingers. You have to find the holes for the fingers for the two front legs. Then you use two fingers to move the mouth up-and-down. Not the easiest thing to do.

The pig “grunts” when you squeeze the “rump” part of the pig. Again, not the best design, in my opinion.

There is a tag that shows that this pig won the 2014 “plush toy” award, which I find very hard to believe.

Finally. . . This is a Made in China toy. . . At the current price it’s WAY too expensive for Made in China.

- Intex The Wet Set Rectangular Pool Cover
- Intex 120V AC Quickfill Pump
- 10'X12' HD Tarp
- Associated pool toys

Set up was made quick and easy by matching the large opening on the pump with each of the three large intake openings on the pool to get all three levels quickly filled with air, starting at the bottom as per the directions. After laying out the tarp the pool unfolded quickly and we centered it over the tarp prior to inflating. We followed the suggestions of other reviewers to use the smaller tip on the pump with the smaller valve openings on the pool to finalize the air fill so as not to over inflate. The entire setup process couldn't have taken more than 15-20 minutes. Very easy.

It took another 20-25 minutes to fill the pool with a garden hose to the fill line clearly marked inside the pool. With a 90 degree day outside in the sun we could have done without adding any hot water but we did put in a couple pots anyway. We also added a cup of household bleach to the pool as one reviewer suggested. Undoubtedly there are better ways of keeping the water clean and we'll research those as we go along. We simply wanted to get up and running quickly the first time as our 5 year old couldn't wait.

Wouldn't have set this pool up any other way. The electric air pump made inflation of the three levels very quick and easy. I would recommend a tarp (they're quite inexpensive at Lowes or Home Depot), and while you could use a bed sheet as a pool cover we're quite satisfied with the Intex product.

Just a reminder - there's a single drain valve in the bottom corner of the pool. Remember to close that prior to filling. I forgot to do it and as I began filling the pool I thought it had arrived with a leak. Doh!

Keep in mind that this is a day 1 review. Cleaning, etc., may dampen our enthusiasm but if this pool lasts through the summer it will have been well worth the investment.

The only complaint we have after our first really fun day with this pool is that Amazon lowered the price by $5 the day after ours arrived. That's the second time this has happened to us with an Amazon purchase. While it's only $5 it is irksome.
text_fidelity_b: Intex Swim Center Family Inflatable Pool, 120" X 72" X 22", for Ages 6+

text_fidelity_a:
Nerf N-Strike Elite Stryfe Blaster (Colors May Vary) I bought 2 of these blasters for my daughter and I. We have Nerf battles in the house and She wanted a semi auto (to back up her Recon and Maverick) and I need a backup for the Hail Fire. This is a clip system balster with a fly wheel launcher (need 4 AA batteries). All in all I'm pretty pleased.
Good: This blaster does a lot of things well. It is a semi-auto (requires 4 AA batteries), but does not feel heavy or unbalanced. Easy to shoot 1 handed and can be double wielded. Clip system is nice as we have a lot of extra clips so reloads are fast. The clip release button has a good positive feel and has not accidentally relesed a clip yet. The blaster has a top and bottom tactical rail and will accecpt a stock and barrel extention (although why you would want to do this is questionable as it takes away the intent of this compact blaster). Handgrip is comfortable but may be to small for XL hands. Accel. button has a good feel to it. There are 2 place for sling attachment and both spots are logical! Battery door is a sigle screw affair. Accuracy is better than expected (I can hit a human size target 5 out of 6 times at a 30 foot range). Battery life has been good and Rechargables offer no problems.
Bad: This blaster has more safety switches than a modern Table Saw! There is the jam door switch, the clip sensor switch, dart sensor switch, voltage switch (regulator), accel trigger switch, and probably others that I haven't come across yet. The main trouble maker is the dart sensor switch. It works great until the last dart in the clip. Sometimes the dart pressure is not enough to press the switch arm so the blaster won't fire the last dart (VERY ANNOYING!) The easiest NONE WARRENTY VOIDING fix is to open the jam door, take a thin (about 1/8" wide) piece of duct tape (about 2 inches long) and tape the switch to the top of the reciever. I taped it up and around the body and out the top of the jam door. After aprox 100 shots the tape is still holding and I have yet to have a dart left in the clip. The gun is also prone to jamming if you pull the trigger slowly. When firing off a dart you need to make sure to pull the trigger crisply. This only seems to be a problem on the first shot (probably because I usually empty the clip after that first shot). Another problem I've seen is the dislike this blaster has for non-elite darts. If your first dart in the clip is a streamline version you can almost be assured a jam (funny that it only happens if the non-elite is in the first position on the clip- load it farther down and it fires like any other dart). Honestly if your gonna use this for any formal matches stick to the Elite darts. Range is about 35 to 40 feet- hard to get any further.
Final thoughts: This is truely a fun blaster. It does have a few kinks to it, but nothing that a little duct tape can't fix. It is compact enough to carry as a secondary blaster, but combined with additional clip options (I'm thinking an 18 with a couple six back-ups) this could be a close quarters primary blaster. At the current $20 this is really a no brainer.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf N-Strike Elite Stryfe Blaster (Colors May Vary)

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Empire Game "Monopoly Empire" is like a simplified version of the traditional game of Monopoly. The colors and layout of the board are very similar to the traditional game, but each has a famous logo, such as Hasbro or EA Sports, instead of street names. The object of the game is to add tiles with various brands to your Times Square type "billboard tower" before the other players. The more brands you add to your billboard, the more money you get when passing Go, which allows you to buy more brands. The game tokens are representative of the brands in the game, such as a bottle of Coca-Cola and an Xbox controller. The board is a bit smaller than the traditional board, because it doesn't have railroads.

The game is easy to learn, in part because of an excellent, full-color instruction guide that includes a very clear diagram of how to set up the board. The way the items are priced make it easy to pay for purchased tiles. Although the game is lacking the excitement and strategy of trading properties and building houses as in the original version of Monopoly, it is good for a quick game. It would be easy for kids to learn and play. The game is most fun when it's a close race between the players to complete their towers. If one player takes a large, early lead, it's hard for the other person to come from behind.

Note: The logoed tiles have various sizes, which is part of the game. However, the sometimes the positioning of the stickers with the logo make it confusing to put them into the tower correctly.

All in all, this is a good game that is easy to play and goes by quickly.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Empire Game

text_fidelity_a:
Name 5 Game This is, hands down, the worst game I have ever played for several reasons that all share a central theme of poorly laid out rules. I will share the 2 most glaring flaws from my experience w/ this gem of a game.

#1 A large portion of the categories are so subjective as to make them unplayable. For example, one of the categories in the game is, "Vacation Destinations." Who is to say that literally anything I say is not a valid answer? I could just name any destination on the planet. Who is to say I DON'T want to vacation in Darfur or at my ex-girlfriend's house? This is just one example, there are literally hundreds of categories where anything you say could be construed as a valid answer. The rules are ambiguous and fall back on self-policing as a substitute for a well thought out set of guidelines. The lack of a set of coherent rules leads to an endless debate about the validity of the players' answers that becomes incredibly boring to watch and incredibly frustrating to participate in.

#2 The arguments over what is and what is not a valid answer aside, an average round of this game takes about 10 minutes to play through. So unless you feel like going through the aggravation of playing more than once, you're not getting much bang for your buck. HOWEVER, it is worth noting that portions of this game can run on ad infinitum; one of the poorly engineered "challenges" in this game is to square off against another team to name as many items w/in the category chosen, obviously the one who runs out of ideas loses the challenge. Sounds like a decent idea, BUT instead of placing a time limit and perhaps writing down as many ideas as you can think of, like w/ Scattergories, this game has you go back-and-forth in a turn-taking verbal manner. The category we squared off w/ was "Foods That Begin With A." My god, the list went on and on for 10 minutes before everyone got bored and just called that round a tie. These challenges will not appear in every game; if you have the bad luck of stumbling into this challenge during your game, I advise you to get out a book or go make a sandwich while the teams face-off.

My advice to those considering this game is to buy Taboo or Scattergories instead. These two games are in the same genre and are time-tested winners w/ a clear set of rules. This game needs to be re-engineered with some attention paid to making the categories more thought-provoking and objective. I would recommend this game for parents with 5 year olds that just want to let their kids mess around and yell out random things for 10 minutes.
text_fidelity_b: Name 5 Game

Fisher-Price Octonauts Sea-Slimed Octopod Playset My boys are currently loving all things Octonauts. Before Christmas arrived, my 3 year old was pretending that Legos were each of the Octonauts. While there's nothing wrong with using his imagination, it was becoming very difficult for us to keep up with exactly which Lego was which Octonaut. He was frustrated at our lack of help when it came to locating a specific piece.

This Octopod has been well loved! As far as characters go, this set only comes with Captain Barnacles. We bought other characters separately to make playing with it more fun, though. It also comes with a container of "sea slime". I dislike this stuff greatly, but my children enjoyed it while it lasted. It didn't make a huge mess, and it's not overly sticky, but touching a piece here and there that escaped from the rest was gross. (Reaching under a bed and feeling cold slime isn't the greatest feeling.) The set even comes with a catapult to throw the sea slime, but I really don't recommend doing that.

Assembly is pretty easy. Several pieces have to snap together, and there's several stickers to put into place, but it happens quickly. Be careful with the stickers. Once you stick them, they're stuck. I have a couple of them the slightest bit crooked, but I couldn't fix it. It uses batteries, but those are already included. There's a button to press to hear sound effects(from the show). I didn't find this horribly annoying, but I do actually like the show.

My only complaint is that the top of the Octopod is hard to close properly. My youngest was very frustrated with it at first, and asked for help with it. It seems he's accepted that it won't close just right at this point, and mostly plays with it with the top open.

Overall, my boys have had great fun playing with it. It's been a great addition to the Gups they also got for Christmas.

text_fidelity_a: Holy Stone HS340 Mini FPV Drones with Camera for Kids 8-12 RC Quadcopter for Adults Beginners with One Key Take Off/Landing, Gravity Sensor, Headless Mode, Waypoint Fly, Throw to Go, Indoor & Outdoor I purchased this mini drone because I purchased a HD175D and wanted to learn how to use a drone before trying a more expensive one. So I read the instructions and got the HS340 working  (hoovering) without too much hassle. I tried using the cell phone and camera portion but that would not work so I just settled with the remote control by itself. This worked fine so I began trying to learn to steer I kept it very basic, no tricks or anything that a kid might want to try indoors. After about 5 minutes of getting used to this tiny drone it hit the wall (4 feet up in the air) and slid down to the floor. I turned it off and redid the start up procedure to get more practice controlling the drone. OH NO!!! all it does now is goes side ways and immediately lunges towards the floor. I can not believe how simple it is to destroy this plastic drone. I am a very cautious adult, thus buying this HS340 so that I would have experience under my belt before using a $150 dollar HS175D ( much better than the HS175) drone. I wanted to buy my HD175D from amazon but the D version was on e-xxx  dot com website for less money (after making an offer) and better camera plus better bearings. Now I see that the return window is closed so I will simply throw this $35 (sale price) dollar paper weight in the trash. I guess I can not in good conscience recommend this drone unless you are prepared to use it only in a space that can not hit a wall at 4 foot height. So not very likely. I am quite disappointed with Holy Stone products overall.

Tokaido Board Game (Base Game) | Strategy Game | Travel Adventure Game | Exploration Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 8+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Funforge Simple, serene and elegant, this is a game like few others in your collection. This one is about a trip through Japan, and has very nice Japanese style artwork that really pops. One look at the box cover will tell you how elegant and evocative this game is, and that really is one of it's finest features.

Gameplay is rather simple. Those who rush ahead to see the sights first certainly get some kind of advantage - they often get first choice of where to go - while those who take their time will have plenty of opportunity to catch up, as the last player is always the next to move, meaning that travellers who venture too far out will allow others to make every stop along the way. There are "safe" and predictable options where you always get two or three points, and there are gambling options where you might be able to buy cards that give you far more.

It's a good, simple game that works well as a gateway game, but like many games, it says it's a decent two-player game, and I don't think that it is. It shines with three to four players. The decisions are not particularly deep or exciting, and much of the time, there really are only two choices that you can choose from - move really slow, or move really fast - and those choices are often easy to make.

If you're a gamer, I don't think you'll like this game. You can find better gateway games for sure, and there are thousands of games where you'll make more interesting choices. If you're just getting into games, or if you need something new to play with grandma, then this might be the best choice you can make.
text_fidelity_b: Tokaido Board Game (Base Game) | Strategy Game | Travel Adventure Game | Exploration Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 8+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Funforge

The kit comes with a few extras - a few minifigs, a small spider minion - but the kit is otherwise entirely made up of the arachnoid mech. Like other Monkie Kid sets, this one is somewhat light on additional characters as opposed to other sets LEGO has made in the past.

Overall, though, this is an impressive kit. It's not terribly challenging, it looks great, it moves well, and it's not particularly dainty to move around. Love it.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Monkie Kid Spider Queen’s Arachnoid Base 80022 Building Kit (1,170 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a: Hands Craft DIY Miniature Dollhouse Kit - Holiday Party Time 3D Model Tiny House Building with LED Lights Wood Prefabricated Pieces Puzzle 1:24 Scale Crafts for Adults and Teens DG153 I like having a variety of crafting types of things around, especially during the winter. I recently heard about these little kits and got a few to try. Books are one of my greatest joys, so I couldn't help but include this one in the mix. I thought they'd be great for doing while I'm listening to an audio book. They're a little different than I thought they'd be, but I do still like them. It comes in a nice little cardboard box, and everything is organized and packaged well. It feels special just opening the box and thinking about the fun challenge ahead, especially with all the little books. In case you're curious, a couple of the books are accordion folded paper, so there are pictures in them, but most are just filled with sponge sheet, so there are no actual pages. Pages would have made it more complicated but would have been cuter. Still, it's a super cute kit, and I like it.

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Games Scrabble Twist Electronic Scrabble Twist is a great idea and it more like an electronic version of Boggle in which players can make as many three, four, or five letter words as possible from a random group of letters before time runs out. Simply press the buttons on the unit to spell the words and “twist” to save the word - the bigger the word, the more points you receive for that word. Unfortunately, I love the idea more than the execution. There are both good and bad features of the game, which I’ve summarized below.

Good:
• Games are quick and rules are basic
• The game can be played by anywhere from 1 to 8 players, depending on the game mode
• There are different games that can be played and different levels of difficulty with varying lengths of the time players are given to find words
• The game quickly shuts off automatically if not in use
• The letters will automatically display in the right direction even if the unit is turned, which is good for the party mode in which the unit is passed and also means it works well for both left and right handed players
• The Turbo mode, for head-to-head play between two or more players is fun
• The sound can be turned off for quieter play

Not So Good:

• The worst part of the game is that the letters are hard to read and is a strain on your eyes after playing for a while. People in my family of all age groups said the same thing.
• Three AA batteries are required, but they’re not included
• The instructions on using the game unit aren’t clear (I was able to figure out how to use it by playing the game a few times.)
• The solo mode tracks high scores, but not by name. It doesn’t feel like you’re working toward anything since you can’t really compare scores from game to game since it depends on the letters you had for each game.
• When the sound is on, it’s loud, even at the lowest level. Different sounds do alert you that you’ve played a valid word. A second sound plays if the word you’ve played is invalid or a duplicate. Sounds also let you know if time is about to run out, but I found that this distracted me from finding my final words
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Games Scrabble Twist

text_fidelity_a:
Repos JUST01 Just One, Various There are a lot of "just one word clues" games out there, from Codenames and Decrypto to games like Funglish, Crosstalk or Word Slam, and this game is yet another to add to that group. I think, however, that it's my secnd favorite of the bunch, and if you need a Codenames Killer, this might be up your alley.

In this team game, one player is attempting to guess a word that the rest of their team knows. Each team member writes down one word only, then compares to see if any matches are detected. If they are, those cards are discarded, and the guesser is left with fewer clues. Therefore, the more obtuse clues you get, the more you'll have, but it can be more difficult to deduce the word than if you're given a few obvious clues.

What I like about this game is that it manages to be a louder than usual team game with secrets. In Codenames or Crosstalk, two previous iterations of the concept, games are fun, but often it's players staring at the board in silence. In this one, you still can't say much, but it does lend itself to quicker play, and it's easier to communicate more freely once you have your clues written since your work is done, and the stress of the round is over for the clue-givers. This is a hard game, and it's definitely a word game, but lends itself to being an excellent family gathering game.
text_fidelity_b: Repos JUST01 Just One, Various

text_fidelity_a:
Forbidden Island – The Cooperative Strategy Survival Island Board Game,2-4 players My wife and I bought this as we are getting more into tabletop gaming (thanks Wil and Felicia!) and I wanted something adventurous and less involved than a city- farm- building simulation game.
This is fairly fun, but the main reason I am writing a review is to specify why I didn't give it four stars and who should get the most enjoyment out of it.
To start out, you choose (randomly for a bit of extra challenge) a character class. These are more realistic classes such as a SCUBA diver, rather than a mage or warrior. Each class has a different special ability, for example the diver can traverse water tiles more easily than other classes. Then you randomly generate the playing field by placing the heavier island cards in a specific formation. Combining the random character roles and the random board is a clever way to make every game different and make sure the players have to think critically rather than relying too much on rote strategies.
Your goal is to traverse the board to collect treasures, cooperating with your fellow players by using each person's ability and the convenience of their position on the board. You may even bail each other out of dire situations by airlifting them to safety or using your special ability, because while you are trying to reach the treasures the island is constantly flooding.
If you ever wanted to play Indiana Jones this is a pretty good start. But for my wife and I to keep it interesting, we have to play on the hardest difficulty level (starting out with more of the island in a flooded state) and even still we have succeeded at our task 100% of the time. Because of this, the game gets old too quickly, which is a shame since the premise is fun, the concept is exciting, the gameplay is perfectly tight, and the artwork is gorgeous.
I do think there is a more appropriate audience for this, which is kids of perhaps 9 years to 13 years playing with other kids or in a mixed group with adults. I think the game will be more challenging for kids and I think playing with kids will make it more fun for the parents/cousins/uncles and aunts etc.
For two adults who are strategy-oriented people, there are more complicated games that are perhaps less beautiful and tightly designed but nonetheless more consistently engaging.
text_fidelity_b: Forbidden Island – The Cooperative Strategy Survival Island Board Game,2-4 players

text_fidelity_a:
Cheerson CX-10 Mini 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis LED RC Quadcopter Toy Drone This is so awesome and it works! I thought that with how affordable it is, that it wouldn't even be able to get off the ground, but it flies great! I have to warn you that it's super hard to fly, though. This will frustrate pretty much everyone except for someone who's already an expert in quad copters. But, it's an awesome first copter to practice on. I felt that I built my skills a lot with this, and now I can fly my bigger copter a lot better than I did before I played around with this.

An awesome thing about this is that you can separately order every part of this copter. And, unlike many electronic devices, the sum of the parts is about the same as getting a new one. So, I guess you could also just get two, and when one breaks, then fix it with the other one. Or wait for them to both break and then Frankenstein a whole one back together. But, because these have such available and interchangeable parts, then I can't give it less than five stars.

The battery lasts for about five minutes of flying. Or, fifteen minutes if you're like me, and get it stuck a lot. And, the blades are all plastic, but they hurt if they run into a person. This is also really easy to get stuck on top of a roof or in a tree, so I recommend flying it in a pretty open field. They do pretty good at crash landings, too, as long as they land on grass, which was most of my landings.

It is packaged with a bunch of replacement blades, too, so you don't have to worry about breaking a few of them. They're easy to replace, too.

This listing has both the CX-10 and CX10A. The only difference is that if you depress the left stick three times on the 10A, then you go into headless mode, which is better for beginners. If you want more control, though, then you should get the CX-10. Or, you should get both, since their parts are all interchangeable.
text_fidelity_b: Cheerson CX-10 Mini 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis LED RC Quadcopter Toy Drone

4DV5 Mini Drone for Kids with 720P Camera,FPV Live Video,LED Lights RC Quadcopter for Beginners,Boys and Girls Toys Gifts, Waypoints, Altitude Hold, Circle Fly,3D Flips,2 Battery,Orange First of all, my 9 year old son LOVED it! The LED lights are amazing and it was easy to watch in the dark at night, or just to enjoy during the day.

The "battery" is very different, you have to hook it up to the black device which has an USB and you need your own adapter to plug and recharge it. Each use lasts maybe 10 minutes max before you need to change batteries and recharge the first one. It is a great way to teach your child to take on different perspectives--if the drone is facing you, your left is actually its' right and your right is it's left. You have to consider that when using the controller just like with RC cars, except it is hard to tell from up in the air. You have to press left or right slightly to figure out which side then rotate it around so you can drive it. It comes with replacement spinners and a small screwdriver.

The return mode is nice, if you are freaking out and afraid it will go into a tree and unable to figure out which way to turn, just press that return button and it will come back to you.

Cons:
1. The drone was able to flip on the first day, but afterwards, for whatever reason, that stopped working. That didn't stop my son from enjoying it.
2. The video/camera app did not work on my phone. I tried different ways to get it to work.
3. Less than a week later, two of the "arms" that connect the ring to the base broke so now it won't lift up correctly. Even with superglue, that didn't help. Unfortunately, it is made of cheap flexible plastic.

So bottom line, I would not recommend buying this item.

This drone is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon.
text_fidelity_b: 4DV5 Mini Drone for Kids with 720P Camera,FPV Live Video,LED Lights RC Quadcopter for Beginners,Boys and Girls Toys Gifts, Waypoints, Altitude Hold, Circle Fly,3D Flips,2 Battery,Orange

text_fidelity_a:
Traxxas 6608 LaTrax Alias Quad-Rotor Ready-to-Fly Helicopter, Assorted Colors The Alias is potentially a great example of the new generation of quadcopters with electronic flight control boards that provide six axis stabilization. When their transmitter control levers are properly trimmed at the beginning of each flight they will hover very stably and are easy to fly even for a beginner.

Unfortunately, LaTrax and Traxxas (LaTrax makes the product and Traxxas provides all customer support) released the Alias before they found a good quality motor that works properly with the Alias. Since the Alias uses four motors and is inoperable if any one of the motors fails this is a major problem.

My Alias flew great for the first two days, but then it became very unstable and flew unpredictably. After only the the sixth or eighth flight one of the motors failed and the Alias would not fly at all.

Traxxas told me the Alias does fly unpredictably when one of its motors is weakening and getting ready to fail. They said they would send me a free replacement motor, but so far it has not arrived. Looking at other Amazon reviews, and on the internet, I see that many other people have also had very early motor failures. I strongly recommend people should not buy the Alias until LaTrax and Traxxas have figured out the early motor failure problem, presumably by finding a better motor.

Update: January 14, 2014

After two initial days of use before one of the motors broke, I have been unable to fly my new Alias for two and a half weeks now. Traxxas keeps saying they will send me a new motor as soon as the most recent batch they received "gets through quality control". I fear I have wasted $150 to buy the Alias.

Update January 20, 2014

After three weeks Traxxas finally sent me a replacement motor ....drum roll.....however, they sent the wrong motor! Traxxas checked their records, agreed they had sent the wrong motor, and promised to send the correct motor. I am pleased they are trying to provide good customer service, but I am now in my fourth week without being able to fly my otherwise excellent Alias after one of its motors broke on the second day after I opened it at Christmas.
text_fidelity_b: Traxxas 6608 LaTrax Alias Quad-Rotor Ready-to-Fly Helicopter, Assorted Colors

Pro
* It looks cool with its sky blue and chrome features, with black seats and slick black wheels. He's the first kid in preschool with a rad set of wheels.

* Steering is actual. The driver could parallel park if needed.
* It auto breaks when the pedal is let go. Nice safety feature.

Con
* Chrome and other parts scratch easily, and even arrived scratched a little

* Seat doesn't move. My boy can barely reach the pedals despite being almost four (the stated age is 4-7). Moving forward, we'll include a back cushion.
* While it too early to be sure, the tires (hollow hard plastic) look like they'll wear quickly.
* I weigh too much. I want to ride in it!

Lots of fun, and a great way to bring your child along on long walks.

Anthony Trendl
treefortbooks.com

text_fidelity_a:
Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome This is a fun ride-on toy for kids. I like that it sits close to the ground, which makes it better for younger kids, but the design is still “cool” enough that older kids will still like it. The dune buggy has a lot of good features. First, the blue color will appeal to both girls and boys. The vehicle has two speeds, which is nice. However, the parent lock-out needs to be removed to access the higher speed. The lock-out is a screw that’s fairly difficult to remove because of its location. The higher speed is definitely needed to easily ride in the wet grass, even on flat ground. It’s fairly easy to steer the vehicle and is a lot of fun for kids to drive.

To stop the vehicle, take your foot off the gas pedal. It will still slide a little on pavement, possibly because of the plastic wheels. It also will continue to slowly roll going downhill, even on a small incline. That’s why even though the guidelines say ages 3 to 7, I would use caution for younger kids unless you have a large, flat area with no nearby hills. Older kids, up to 11 or 12, will like it, too. However, with the position of the steering wheel, their height will determine how well they’ll comfortably fit in the dune buggy and be able to easily steer.

Be sure to charge the battery the night before using the first time. The battery only lasted about 15 minutes right out of the box after being putting the car together. I also learned the hard way that the dune buggy is heavy to push if it does bog down or if the battery dies. (The battery is rechargeable battery, but there isn’t a battery indicator, so I wasn’t expecting it to go dead so quickly.)

Once the dune buggy is assembled and the battery is charged, it’s a lot of fun for kids. The assembly is a chore for adults, though. I took almost an hour and a half to assemble. Most of that time was spent putting on the wheels. The directions aren’t clear and some of the screws are hard to get to and there isn’t room to use an electric screwdriver. As long as you allow enough time for assembly and charging the battery, this dune buggy will be a hit.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome

KidKraft Deluxe Let's Cook Kitchen, Gift for Ages 3+ It really is all it's cracked up to be! I have been eyeing it for almost two years and I got lucky and found it in November for $120. I waited to put it together until the night Santa stopped by our house. It did take a few hours to assemble but my husband never left his recliner. I only needed an extra set of hands once or twice and my mom easily did the job.

The top is tricky to attach because the freezer and microwave doors have a tendency to want to leap off the kitchen. I definitely recommend assembling on carpet--the freezer door fell off while I were attaching the top (it's totally stable after the top is attached) and my hardwood floors dinged the corner when the door landed.

If I had to put the kitchen together again, I would definitely get an Allen wrench drill-bit for my drill. The two types of Allen screws in the box have the same head so you can take one of them to the hardware store to ensure the proper drill bit fit. Using a low-power drill makes furniture assembly fast and SO much more pleasant. :)

My son loves it!!! He was only 18 months at Christmas so I was worried he wouldn't know what to do with a kitchen. To my surprise, he ran right to the stove and started turning knobs. He tested the sink handles to make sure they turned and then he started cooking! I totally recommend the utensils and stainless pots & pans from Ikea (they fit the burners perfect). The Melissa & Doug wooden pantry and fridge foods are awesome, as well. Very, very cute.

All-in-all, I am completely delighted with the quality and playtime potential this kitchen offers. My baby might not have any idea what I am talking about when we play "Iron Chef", but he knows how to stir, flip, move things to the sink and move food from the fridge to the microwave to the oven...

Oh, also, my big little guy is 33" already and he has to stand on his tip-toes to see inside his stock pot. He will be cooking for many years to come.
text_fidelity_b: KidKraft Deluxe Let's Cook Kitchen, Gift for Ages 3+

Learning Resources Botley The Coding Robot - 45 Pieces, Ages 5+ Screen- Free Coding Toys, Coding STEM Toy for Kids, Coding for Kids,Back to School Gifts,Teacher Supplies Botley is quite a versatile fellow.

My four year old is having fun running him around in "line" mode, where his sensors follow a black lined path on a white background. When he reaches the end, he turns around and comes back.

Daddy is having a little more fun with "code" mode, which is too complex for the little one at this point. You program multiple commands into the remote, and then you send Botley out on a small adventure, around the obstacle course pieces that you can set up with material from the box. It's simple and easy for an adult, but for kids, it will teach computer programming basics, planning ahead, and thinking before you act.

The box comes with a variety of cones, bricks and blocks, as well as arms for Botley and cards that can help you measure how far he's going to move, and doubles as a wavy black line pattern on the reverse side if you want to use it. All told, it's a fun and complete package, although I wish the instructions were a little more explicit for adults, and a little more fun for little ones to explore on their own. As it stands, the manual explains a few little tasks you can try, written in tiny font in as few pages as humanly possible. I want more from this.

Being more than a month away, I was worried the worms wouldn't make it for the holidays. I contacted the seller right away to get tips on how to keep the worms alive and they were not helpful at all. I think I got a one or two sentence reply with no information. So I decided to do some research myself and I was able to keep them all alive without having to transfer them until the farm was opened on Christmas day. I kept them in the dark and a cool area of my house. I would take the cup out once a week to check on them. I'd water the soil a little every other week (just moist, not wet). I also set a couple carrot shavings, a torn up spinach leaf, and a broken egg shell on the top.  The worms did really well.  We transferred them as soon as she opened the farm.  The farm itself was disappointing in size and much smaller than I was expecting. It's more like the size of holding your two hands side by side. We plan to transfer them from the farm to her vermicompost bin in a few weeks.  She seems happy with the purchase, but overall I would not recommend this farm and would suggest creating your own with a little more research.
text_fidelity_b: Nature Gift Store Kids Worm Farm Observation Kit Shipped with Live Worms

TAMIYA Models Chi Ha Type 97 Tank (Japanese) This tank model is superlative with a lot of details to glue on. ( it has no unnecessary steps that one hates and all the details are easy to glue on and there is no awkward steps that will make one curse while doing it) It take more than the time you expected which for an experienced modeler that is a joy t o add one after another small piece to the model and make it looks very real. After it is done it looks like from a $40 dollar kit than a 16 doller kit.
I have always learned something from other people's comment about how a model is made. Here I am going to recommend using epoxy glue for small parts of plastic details. The epoxy glue gives you more time than CA glue for small detail pieces. And the epoxy glue also have thicker substance than CA glue for small pieces so it will stay in place when the small pieces are glued on. The epoxy glue also becomes thicker as time goes on so you can adjust your timing to chose the right time to glue the pieces on to the model. The smaller the pieces the faster you need to glue on the model and the larger piece you can wait until is becomes very thick before using it. Another trick about dealing with those shining drops left unintentionally on the models; I usually drop some power ( you can use fine grain white pepper dust) onto the drop of glue before it is dried. This will eliminate those ugly sheen of glue and later the glued dust can be painted as rust for weathering.
All in all this little model (about 6 inches long) is well worth your money. It looks far better than other 16 dollar model kits and i can guarantee it.
text_fidelity_b: TAMIYA Models Chi Ha Type 97 Tank (Japanese)

text_fidelity_a:
Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch I'm going to review this not from the perspective of a toy, but rather as a piece of movie memorabilia. Years ago, I use to love to go to the local mall here in Austin and stop by the SunCoast Motion Picture Company store. Where you could buy all sort of movie related items as well as the movies themselves. Over the years I've bought a number of items very similar to this Rocket Raccoon figure for my collection. So when I was offered one of these 10 inch figure to check out I gladly accepted.

I wasn't expecting this figure to be so big - I knew it was suppose to be 10" but it seems bigger than that to me. It came in one of those open face boxes that allow you to actually touch the toy before taking it out of the box, and you can activate the sound effect as the item ships with the batteries already installed and the sound box is set in a demo mode. The sounds it make are pretty loud, they should put a smile on any child face (and a frown on any adults in the room).

Once out of the box, there is some assembly required. You have to pop the tail into the figures rear-end (yeah, I know). It takes some effort to do that, so I suggest having an adult do it. Other than that, the figure is ready to go. Like I mentioned there is a demo mode on the effects box. The effects are controlled with a three-position switch - Off, Try Me (demo), and On. The unit is powered by three double-A batteries which are located in the figures backpack (there is a screw securing the cover to the batteries). Once you turn on the power switch, there are two activation points - one on the figures leg and another on top of the gun he is holding. Pressing one or the other activates both motion and sound effects, plus the figure speaks phrases from the movie. The motion effects are just the end of the gun rotating and the figure shaking a bit. There are some light effects with the end of the gun & gun sight lighting up. There aren't that many spoken phrases - so they can get a bit repetitive after awhile.

The toy is pretty well made - a lot more substantial than most of the movie memorabilia, but then again it was made for kids to play with.

I kept the figure on my desk at work for about a week before bringing it home. I can't tell you how times people stopped and played with the figure (too many times, as that is what prompted me to finally take it home). I haven't seen the movie yet - but it is definitely one that I plan on seeing this summer.

I really like this figure - about the only thing I could comment on would be the detail of the end of his gun, everything else has a decent level of detail, but that part of the gun doesn't. Guessing that is more due to the fact that they made it out of clear plastic so that the light effect could be seen.
text_fidelity_b: Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch

Know a bunch of words? Short ones? Long ones? Skinny ones? Know any big fat words you just can't use anywhere else? Use them here. Show off how big your vocabulary is, and that you know how to use it. Of course, there are rules about which ones count, but mostly, regular words are OK. Just nothing with capitals or foreign words, unless of course, you are from somewhere else, but then, they aren't foreign any longer, are they?

Order up a serving of Scrabble. Figure out if you need this version or the deluxe version (which is mighty cool.) If you are new to Scrabble, this is the version to start with.

When you get the game in the mail, call up some friends, turn on some tunes, crack open something tasty and cold, and start munching a few chips. This ain't a game you gotta be smart to play. I've seen guys who only know small words, but they could see the best ways to use them. Vocabs don't win the game. Thinking on your feet will win the game.

I fully recommend Scrabble.
